sections.content:
Let me analyze what happened:
1. The right panel is now all gray (g) - all 9 squares are gray
2. The upper structure changed - the blue element at the right end (originally b+S) is now just b(2 pixels) + S(2 pixels) - much smaller
3. The green bar on the right edge (id=2, color=N, 116 pixels) is still there
Looking at the upper structure:
- Original: b(14) + S(16) + g(76) + b(8) + S(8)
- Now: b(14) + S(16) + g(88) + b(2) + S(2)
The right end blue/sky blue elements shrank from 8+8=16 pixels to 2+2=4 pixels. The gray bar grew from 76 to 88 pixels (gained 12 pixels).
So the mechanic seems to be:
- Clicking white squares in the right panel turns them green
- When all 4 cross-position white squares are clicked (turned green), they all reset to gray
- The upper structure's right-end elements shrink when the panel is "completed"
Maybe the goal is to continue this process - click more squares to shrink the upper structure further? Or maybe I need to click on gray squares now?
Let me think about this differently. The upper structure has a blue/sky blue element on the left and a smaller one on the right. Maybe the goal is to transfer the right element to the left, or vice versa?
Let me try clicking on the gray squares in the right panel now to see what happens.
